behaviors.behavior: The legacy-fallback branch's claim-authorized launch carries the allow-list and permission-mode on every shell form, and excludes Task/WebFetch

behaviors.behavior: Template arming fails closed when the --session-id anchor appears more than once in the rendered command (Stage-2 code-review HIGH finding)

behaviors.behavior: templateDeclaresSessionIdAnchor correctly detects the literal --session-id {task.uuid} placeholder in a raw (pre-substitution) command_template, and correctly rejects templates without it

A claim-authorized launch against a custom project action whose command_template has no --session-id anchor at all is refused with 409, over a real HTTP request through the real route + a real temp-directory actions.json

behaviors.behavior: Stage-3 doubt-review attack: a template with NO real --session-id anchor is still refused (409) even when a caller-supplied description is crafted to coincidentally contain the literal anchor text — proves the template-source check, not just the rendered-output check, is load-bearing
behaviors.evidence: action-substitution-branch.claim-permission.test.ts: 'a template with NO --session-id {task.uuid} placeholder is refused even when a caller-supplied description coincidentally contains the literal anchor text'

surface_verification.justification: Backend-only permission-perimeter change to POST /api/external/tasks/:id/launch, no UI surface. The security-relevant behavior (which command string the route returns to the caller) is exercised directly by real Hono app.request() integration tests against the actual router (not mocked internals) in claim-permission-perimeter-centralized.test.ts and action-substitution-branch.claim-permission.test.ts, including a real temp-directory .shipwright-webui/actions.json for the custom-template attack scenarios — this is the wire-level contract a live-server probe would additionally exercise. Small complexity; F0.5 is advisory, not mandatory, below medium.
